races.name: Edinburgh Childrens Hospital Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has found only five or six horses over 10f on Good recently; today's step up to 1m5f on matching ground is a positive but his trainer's 14-day strike rate of 4/10 and a 26-day absence give mild concern, and tongue-tie headgear suggests he needs things to fall right late.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Withington's best recent effort was a third five starts back, and he has done little since to build on it — yet he arrives fit at 26 days, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 56 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: The race's pivotal figure — two recent wins at 10f and 12f onStandside confirm his form but today he steps back out to 1m5f where his sole run at that trip produced a pulled-up result; Kevin Stott takes the ride for Iain Jardine whose 14-day return of 2/22 is modest, and his STYLE_FIT flag reminds us he's racing at the outer limit of his comfortable range.|
runners_data.comment: Gemini Man won three of his last six starts, including back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and going — a genuine threat at 135 lb. The concern is his latest two outings: a pull-up and a ninth last time out suggest his form has dipped sharply.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type who showed placed ability at 12f on Good going but his three runs at 16f produced two sevenths and an eighth, casting real doubt on his ability to see out today's extra distance; the addition of a hood (hg:b) and David Nolan's experience are positives, but the trip concern is genuine.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has been placed three times in his last five starts, most recently a second 24 days ago — he has run over today's trip and going and arrives fit. The risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old mare with an outstanding recent placed record — seven placed finishes from nine runs on Good going is exceptional consistency — but she operates at shorter trips mostly (8-12f) and steps up markedly to 1m5f here; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim helps offset her top weight burden somewhat, though trainer R Mike Smith has had zero winners from 16 runners over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Sophiesticate has been consistent without threatening the lead, posting thirds in her last three starts, though a sixth and seventh before that temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going, and 11 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough, but she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Carries a noted tendency to fade in the closing stages, which is a significant concern over this extended 1m5f trip; her best recent form at 12f on Good (4th) flatters a little given the pattern of weakening, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim doesn't fully compensate — her true hold-up nature means she'll be coming from further back than the map position suggests.|

runners_data.name: Ivynator
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose recent form figures of P/5-00 paint a bleak picture, and her simulated-going record shows only 1 placing from 13 Good-ground runs — a damning statistic for today; held up naturally, Jean McGregor's yard has had no runners in 14 days providing no recent form guide, and 35 days off adds to the questions.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up on one of those occasions, Ivynator arrives 35 days fresh with experience of today's trip and going to call on — though the main concern is that unplaced efforts dominate his recent form, and 130 lb is a stiff burden at an official mark of 48.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: Recent form of 430493 contains enough placed efforts to keep interest alive, and his 14-day return of 14 days is fine; he goes in blinkers (hg:b) which tends to sharpen him, and Liam Bailey's team have shown he stays 14f on Standside — although today's Good going at Musselburgh is a fresh test and Billy Garritty's record on him will be key to whether he can travel close enough to matter.|
runners_data.comment: Yakhabar has placed third last time out — and was fourth three starts back — but has gone winless in his last six starts, and that ninth two starts back is a concern; experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no surprises.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: A four-year-old who has been admirably consistent — four second-place finishes in recent starts, all over 12-13f on Good or Good-to-Soft — and today's step to 1m5f looks within range for a horse who has been knocking firmly on the door; Greg Fairley takes the ride for trainer Katie Scott, who has 1 winner from 8 runners over 14 days, and the visor (hg:v) is a feature to note given he's worn it throughout his placed run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts despite a clutch of runner-up finishes, Falaise Blanc heads here ranked seventh of nine on our figures and carries 128 lb; he has run over today's trip and going, which offers some grounding, but it's hard to look past a woeful official mark of 46.

runners_data.name: Liberty Looming
runners_data.note: Five-year-old returning from an 81-day absence for Adam Nicol's small yard (0 winners from 2 runners in 14 days), and his form figures at 16-17f on Good show only two faded efforts before back-to-back fifths last season; genuine hold-up type who needs everything to fall perfectly after a long layoff, which looks unlikely here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts — two fourths and two unplaced efforts — Liberty Looming also returns after 81 days off, and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, he's hard to fancy despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Star Of Markinch
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old whose record of four fourth-place finishes in his last five runs at 12-16f on Good ground shows remarkable consistency at a level — though it's the consistency of a horse who rarely wins; 56 days since his last run is a minor concern, and Oisin McSweeney will need to get him well-positioned to have any impact on the principals.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a sequence of fourths and worse, Star Of Markinch heads into this off a 56-day absence ranked bottom on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going, but little else in the profile suggests she can reverse her fortunes here.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m5f handicap and, with no genuine rival willing or able to push him for the lead, he will stride out from the gates and control a comfortable, sustainable gallop around Musselburgh's flat track. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up horses — Mr Withington, Jedhi Knight, Sophiesticate, Storm On Jura, Ivynator, Yakhabar, Falaise Blanc, Liberty Looming and Star Of Markinch are all natural hold-up or wait-and-see types, meaning they will fan out behind Gemini Man and queue up for a finishing run in the straight. Because so many true hold-up horses populate the rear, the race map redistributes several of them into midfield slots, but this should not be confused with genuine prominent intent — they will still be chasing Gemini Man's tail rather than pressing him. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate, with Yakhabar, Storm On Jura and Falaise Blanc among those most capable of tracking closer than their natural style, though none constitutes a true pace rival to Gemini Man. This race shape — a lone leader setting a measured, unflustered gallop over a staying trip on Good ground — strongly favours horses that can travel economically in midfield before delivering a sustained late run, with any horse that can get a prominent position just off the pace holding a significant tactical advantage over the deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gemini Man Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man leads at his own tempo and no rival has the ability or inclination to seriously press him through the race.
scenarios.body: Gemini Man dictates a honest but not punishing gallop, conserves enough energy to hold on into the straight, and his recent winning form at this sort of trip and going underpins his chance of lasting home; horses that can travel just off the pace in second or third will be best positioned to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses manage to travel just behind Gemini Man throughout and produce a sustained challenge from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With a moderate pace set by a single front-runner over 1m5f, any horse that can lock onto Gemini Man's girth from the outset avoids traffic and saves significant ground; Falaise Blanc's consistent placed form at 12f on Good and Sophiesticate's relentless placed record both point to this profile suiting them best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Get Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough to compress the field, creating a bunched finish where late runners can thread through gaps in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo and a tight, crowded pack through the middle stages can allow a horse with a sharp late turn of foot to weave through tired rivals; Yakhabar and Jedhi Knight both carry placed form over today's trip on Good ground and have the profile to benefit if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Deep Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man is pushed harder than expected or sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns him out before the straight, leaving the race open to the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: This shape requires Gemini Man to fold and the furthest-back horses to deliver a sweeping run, a combination unlikely given his lone-lead advantage and the hold-up bias of his rivals who would need to race out of their natural positions; Mr Withington or Star Of Markinch could theoretically collect if chaos ensues.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Yakhabar, Falaise Blanc or Sophiesticate manages to slot in just behind Gemini Man in the early stages — whoever secures that position off a single pace-setter over 1m5f holds a major tactical edge over the deep closers.|

Gemini Man's lone front-running role is central to the race shape — if he shows any sign of distress or is hassled in the first half-mile by a rival racing out of character, the entire pace dynamic collapses and opens the race up to unpredictable outcomes.|

Storm On Jura's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a live danger to punters who may back her on a top-four recent form line — over this extended trip with a hold-up style, her weakening pattern looks likely to be exposed again.|

Liberty Looming returns from 81 days off for a small yard with minimal recent runners — monitor her market move and paddock condition closely, as an unexplained confidence support would be worth noting given the layoff.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses creating a congested midfield group means traffic incidents and pocketed runners in the straight are a real possibility — horses with wide draws or jockeys who commit early to the outside rail (Falaise Blanc, Jedhi Knight) may gain a tactical advantage at the top of the straight.|

races.name: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Roger Fell with Kevin Stott aboard; four runs all on Good and placed just once, over 7f at this same trip, with OR 64 suggesting modest ability — needs a clean last-furlong sprint but lacks the form figures to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Bigalo shaped with promise when second last time out, and has run over today's trip and going — his profile makes him a strong each-way threat from stall 2, with our rating of 71 underlining his claims; the concern is that he's been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: Oisin McSweeney rides for Adrian Keatley; a genuine closer stepping up from 6f to 7f for the first time, having run 4-6-6 in similar Good conditions — the trip extension is the key unknown and 43 days since last run adds rustiness risk.
runners_data.comment: Boutblummintime arrives here 43 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him comfortably clear of his six rivals. Fourth last time out, he's winless in recent starts but the figures suggest he's overdue to make his mark from stall 5 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Aurora Valkyrie
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's juvenile showed a placed effort over this exact 7f on Good in its most recent start, and Connor Beasley gives the partnership strong northern representation; a natural hold-up horse whose best chance arrives if the field bunches and a gap materialises late — style-fit note tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a fifth two starts back and a lowly eighth three starts back making her hard to fancy, Aurora Valkyrie does at least return after 25 days with distance and going experience to call on, though she faces a stiff task from stall 6 on a mark of 61.

runners_data.name: Liveadream
runners_data.note: Form figures of 2nd over 7f Good and 4th over 7f Soft mark this as the most trip-proven horse in the field; Phillip Makin's runner is very fresh on a 7-day turnaround and, while naturally a closer, may be pressed more positively by Harry Russell given the lack of any true front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Liveadream shaped with promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; at 131 lb and yet to win in her last four starts, she'll need to find more than that placed effort suggests.

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's high-volume yard sends out a horse with five runs showing 3rd-3rd consistency over 7-8f on Good; runs in a hood (hg:p) which may aid focus, and five runs on similar going make the conditions no issue — but OR 51 is the lowest in the field and the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five, Tiger In The Tree does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and back-to-back thirds give her a platform; a rating of 62 suggests more ability than her official mark of 51 implies, though stepping up from that level remains the test.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly is the most credentialled horse here — a winner over 7f on Good with an OR of 62 and the form sequence 086612 showing progressive improvement; Ben Robinson can press forward if needed, giving Amantha the tactical flexibility that every other runner in this hold-up-heavy field lacks.
runners_data.comment: Amantha shaped well last time out, finishing second, and followed up a win two starts back — she has experience over today's trip and going, and stall one could prove interesting. The concern is her trainer's current run of 0 from 26 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood (hg:b) for Phillip Makin and wears the same colours as stablemate Liveadream — Billy Garritty rides a horse whose 2nd over 7f on Standard and 4th over 6f on Good show she handles pace variations; a true hold-up type who needs the race to be truly end-to-end, which this shape is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Bluestone Lady nevertheless showed ability with a second two runs back, and she has run over today's distance and going before; ranked sixth of seven on our figures, however, she faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 132 lb.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner nursery, the early gallop is likely to be set by default rather than design, meaning whoever settles best from the gates may drift into a position slightly ahead of their natural inclination. The entire field is catalogued as hold-up types, which means the race is likely to be run at a muddling or modest tempo before erupting into a scrambling sprint finish over the final two furlongs at Musselburgh. Amantha, Aurora Valkyrie, Bluestone Lady, Liveadream, Tiger In The Tree, Bigalo, and Boutblummintime are all genuine hold-up or come-from-behind operators, and none can genuinely dictate — the field holds more true hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Amantha and Liveadream (recent form figures suggesting positional awareness) most likely to actually push forward and secure a prominent berth if anything. The tactical verdict is clear: this race strongly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot and the ability to sprint late from a compact midfield group, with the best-quality closer finding the most daylight from the final turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts along at an honest-but-uncontested tempo and bunches into a late dash up the Musselburgh straight.
scenarios.body: No single horse controls the tempo so the pack compresses, meaning horses with a clinical late kick and good form on Good ground will dominate the final furlong; the sprint finish suits those who travel smoothly in a tight group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Amantha Quickens From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Amantha — a winner over 7f at Musselburgh on similar Good ground — is pushed forward to lead or sit second and dictates a rail-hugging gallop.
scenarios.body: Having already won over course-relevant conditions with Ben Robinson and carrying class form figures of 2-1, she would be ideally placed to kick clear before rivals can respond; a steady early pace into a strong Musselburgh straight suits a horse who can travel and quicken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Liveadream Stalks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Liveadream is ridden positively just off a slow pace and times a run from second or third to the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Phillip Makin's runner is fresh off a 7-day turnaround having shown a placed effort over this exact 7f trip, and with Harry Russell able to press forward if needed, a clean passage into the straight would be decisive; Liveadream's recent 2nd over 7f on Good suggests the trip and ground are firmly in its favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early few furlongs are genuinely dawdled and a wave of finishers overwhelms those trying to make the running.
scenarios.body: While Bigalo and Boutblummintime are true hold-up types who would benefit from a strong late sectional, their style-fit concerns and modest OR ratings make a dominating late surge less probable; this scenario requires an unusually compressed finish and clean runs for every closer.

watchPoints.text: Amantha is the lone runner with a win in her recent form and has already proven herself over 7f on Good — if Ben Robinson presses forward early to fill the leadership vacuum, she becomes the horse to beat in almost every scenario.

Liveadream runs just seven days after its last start — monitor market moves pre-race, as Phillip Makin stabling two runners (with Bluestone Lady) could signal a stable confidence angle on one over the other.

Tiger In The Tree is the lowest-rated horse in the field at OR 51 and races in a hood, but Tim Easterby's yard runs at a T14 strike rate of 7/91 — sheer volume masks form, and this runner's consistent placed efforts over 7f on Good could be misread as progression when it may be a ceiling.

With all seven horses catalogued as hold-up types, watch for a slow, scrappy break from the gates — any horse that jumps cleanly and secures an uncontested position in the first two furlongs gains a structural advantage that may not be apparent from style labels alone.

Bluestone Lady's 0-from-7 run on Good ground (sim-going 4/7 with no wins) is the weakest ground profile in the field — if the Good surface rides quick late in the evening card, discount her chance accordingly.

races.name: Bernard Hunter Metal Recycling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner who has placed twice on good ground and brings strong course form, though 96 days off is a notable flag and the trainer's recent strike rate of 1/6 tempers confidence; the confirmed lead is its biggest asset but it has to do it all from the front in a small field.
runners_data.comment: Jer Batt has been placed three times in his last five starts, most recently third, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid profile as the top-rated runner here; 96 days off is a watch, but at 136 lb from stall four he retains clear claims.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Michael Dods-trained three-year-old with two wins from ten on good ground over five furlongs and strong recent form reading 153 — comfortably the best recent performer here; a natural hold-up type whose task is to find enough room and momentum to close on a front runner given a soft lead in a five-runner race.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Magnus arrives fresh on 27 days' rest with distance and going experience in his favour, and that win three starts back underlines his ability to deliver on the day; the concern is he has been held to third or worse in his two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Francisco's Piece
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley runner returning after 52 days, with a deeply uninspiring recent record of 0 wins and 0 places from seven runs on good going; the horse's natural closer style is at a structural disadvantage in this race shape, and the form string of 005-75 offers little encouragement regardless of pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Francisco's Piece nevertheless carries an 85 rating into this and has run over today's trip and going — the back-to-back fifths either side of a seventh two starts back suggest consistency of a kind, though converting that into a finish is the obvious concern after 52 days off.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's prominent racer has won and placed multiple times on good ground over five furlongs including a course win, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim brings the weight down to 132lbs; positioned ideally to track Jer Batt and mount a challenge in the final furlong, making this horse the key tactical beneficiary of the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Montezuma shaped well when third last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat from stall two on 132 lb; the main concern is that he has found one or more rivals too strong in recent starts, and our rating suggests he may be marginally exposed in this company.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse — recent winner over this course and trip — whose true closing style places it at a positional disadvantage in a five-runner field where the rear is already crowded; Kevin Stott is a capable jockey to find a gap, but the horse's redistribution to midfield on the map reflects a real-world problem of too many closers chasing too few lengths of daylight in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures, and his record of one win in his last six starts — albeit that success came last time out — makes him hard to fancy at the weights carrying 130 lb; has run over today's trip and going, which at least is something.

races.paceDynamic: Jer Batt is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a five-runner field, should be able to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop over Musselburgh's straight five furlongs. Montezuma is the only other prominent-style horse and will likely track Jer Batt in second, meaning the pace is set by one horse rather than multiple rivals fighting for position — a controlled, metronomic tempo rather than a burning early fraction. With the pace sustainable and the race run in a single file, hold-up horses Mighty Magnus and Francisco's Piece will need to produce strong late finishes from the rear, but on good ground over five furlongs the time to close ground is limited, which favours those who can race prominently without being overextended early. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Curious Rover is a true closer but has been mapped to midfield, and it is Mighty Magnus who is best-credentialled to access a forward pitch if circumstances allow; this race shape ultimately tilts in favour of the prominent runner tracking the pace, as an unchallenged leader over a tight five furlongs on good ground gives hold-up horses very little margin for error.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Track And Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt sets a sustainable lead and Montezuma tracks unopposed to challenge entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Jer Batt dictates a fair but uncontested pace, and Montezuma, having conserved energy in second, is perfectly placed to strike when the leader ties up; on good ground at Musselburgh this track-and-challenge dynamic is the dominant shape in small-field five-furlong sprints. The front two pull clear of the hold-up horses who simply cannot generate enough momentum from an orthodox rear position in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is misjudged or Jer Batt idles in front, creating a sprint finish that allows late runners to close.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace compresses the field and the final furlong becomes a cavalry charge, giving Mighty Magnus or Curious Rover the speed they need to reel in the leaders; Mighty Magnus's two wins on good ground over this exact trip make him the standout beneficiary of this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt finds an extra gear in the final furlong and the hold-up horses face a wall of pace too hot to reel in.
scenarios.body: Jer Batt, given a soft lead and upped tempo mid-race, capitalises on the absence of any pressing rival and galvanises the front-runner's advantage as the race enters its closing stages; on good ground with no pressure to burn it out early, a genuine front runner can still score.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Delivers Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and Francisco's Piece, fresh off a 52-day break, produces an unexpectedly strong late run.
scenarios.body: Francisco's Piece has poor form on good ground and no recent wins in this trip-and-surface combination, making this a low-probability scenario reliant on everything going wrong for the principals; only a complete change in the race's tempo architecture would bring this horse into contention at the business end.

watchPoints.text: Montezuma — if Lauren Young gets a clean track directly behind Jer Batt from stall draw, this horse is ideally positioned to challenge and overturn the front runner in the final 100 yards; watch for an unimpeded passage from the gates.

Jer Batt — 96 days off the track combined with a trainer in modest form (1/6 over 14 days) raises fitness questions; if it ties up after setting the pace, the race unravels for everyone tracking it too.

Mighty Magnus — two wins on this exact trip and going make it a live threat, but it must find cover and then clear space in a five-runner field where the prominent horses will be filling the gaps ahead; watch whether Connor Beasley elects to push forward rather than accept a rear position.

Curious Rover — recent course winner over course and distance, but its redistribution to midfield reflects a genuine structural issue; if the pace is genuinely slow and the field compresses, Kevin Stott may attempt to grab a prominent pitch early and race outside its natural comfort zone.

Francisco's Piece — watch the betting market for any significant move; the form and going figures are poor, but a 52-day break with a fresh yard angle and an apprentice booking could signal stable confidence that the bare form does not reflect.

races.name: East Air Conditioning Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner here at Musselburgh who shapes to dictate from the off on good ground she handles well (12 from 15 similar-going runs); eight-year-old carrying 135lbs and racing prominently rather than in a pure lead role per her style tag, but in practice she is the pace in this field and her chance hinges entirely on whether that unchallenged lead proves decisive.|
runners_data.comment: Braes Of Doune holds the highest rating in this field and has run over today's trip and going, while 18 days gives him a fresh but race-fit look from stall three; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts, with a pair of sixths most recently.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer with good recent form at this course and trip, placing twice at 7f on good ground; James Sullivan rides and the Ruth Carr yard has hit 3/20 over 14 days, adding some confidence, and his sim-going record of 9/15 suits — the main question is whether he can close enough ground off a slow gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Consecutive seconds two and three starts back show King Sharja has the class to threaten here, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset at 135 lb from stall six; yet to land it in recent starts, and that unplaced effort last time is the note of caution.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up type bumped forward in the mapping because of the glut of closers in this field — do not take his midfield position at face value, as he will likely race towards the rear; four placings from 10 similar-going runs but no wins, and his STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations if he cannot get his preferred late-running shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Monhammer does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second three starts back shows he can threaten — but a sixth last time out and our rating sitting above his official mark of 48 suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old arrives on 15 days' rest and wears headgear; she is a true hold-up horse pressed into a midfield slot on the map purely because so many closers fill this field — her recent form shows consistent placing (including a second at 7f on good) and she could push forward earlier than her natural style dictates, which may suit if the gallop is gentle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Misemerald is hard to fancy despite some consistency — third and second in recent starts suggest she finds a way to be competitive, and she has run over today's trip and going before from stall one carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type for Liam Bailey running just nine days after her last start, with her best form coming over shorter trips at six furlongs; her sim-going record is modest (6/13) and the step back up to 7f on Musselburgh's track is a mild concern — mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up horse, her true running style is from off the pace where gaps are not always guaranteed.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of her last two starts, Wait For It arrives here just nine days on from her most recent effort in fine heart. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a speed rating of 61 suggests she has more ability than her official mark of 45 implies, though she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's five-year-old hold-up filly whose recent form at this course is limited (3 from 5 on similar going, no wins), and most of her placed runs have come over shorter distances of five to six furlongs; a 13th on her most recent good-ground run at 6f is a red flag, though Greg Fairley's tactical nous in traffic could matter if the straight becomes congested.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with only a single runner-up finish to show, April Diamond is hard to fancy stepping back in after an unplaced effort 25 days ago; she has run over today's trip and going, and stall two is her lot at 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old — a winner at 7f on Tapeta — arrives 17 days fresh with a promising form string including a recent third at this trip on good; genuinely a hold-up type redistributed to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, meaning Connor Beasley may push him forward to claim a better pitch, and his sim-going record (2/15) is thin but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/45 keeps expectations measured.|
runners_data.comment: Sanditon showed his best when winning four starts back, and he arrives here on a handy 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions. The concern is his inconsistency, with fifth last time out following a seventh two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-furlong handicap at Musselburgh and, facing no genuine pace rival, should stride into an uncontested lead from the off and set a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground. The remainder of the field — King Sharja, Monhammer, Misemerald, Wait For It, April Diamond and Sanditon — are all natural hold-up types, meaning Braes Of Doune dictates terms entirely on her own terms with no pressure to inflate the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel comfortably in behind a single leader before mounting a late challenge, but crucially, with so many closers in the field, they will compete against each other for the same ground in the straight. The field holds far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Sanditon and Misemerald, both tagged as redistributed, are the most likely to push forward and secure a prominent position closer to Braes Of Doune than their natural style suggests, which could prove advantageous if the pace is modest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Lone Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune leads unchallenged and the pack fails to close quickly enough off a controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune sets a comfortable fractions-controlled pace throughout the seven furlongs, and with no horse willing to go with her early, she conserves enough to hold on as closers arrive late but flat. Prominent-to-lead profiles who can race close to a single, unhurried pace-setter without getting caught wide are most rewarded here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune's lead is sufficient to set a deceptively honest pace and the hold-up horses find clear runs to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: The closers track a moderate leader and, with clear lanes opening in the straight, the best-finishing hold-up types pounce in the final furlong as Braes Of Doune ties up. King Sharja and Monhammer have the form profiles to benefit from a late surge on good ground at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Sanditon or Misemerald push forward from their redistributed midfield maps to race prominently and outbattle the hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: Either Sanditon or Misemerald, both genuine hold-up horses who are likely to push closer than their mapped positions suggest, secure a pitch just behind Braes Of Doune and sustain their effort into the straight before the true hold-up runners can accelerate. Sanditon's previous Musselburgh course form and Charlie Johnston's 14-day record give this marginal credibility, though both runners are racing somewhat out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of hold-up types causes congestion, interference or wide runs in the straight, gifting the race to whoever finds daylight first.
scenarios.body: With five or six horses all tracking the same lonely leader and all making their move simultaneously, gaps close and multiple closers fail to produce their finish, leaving the race to the one fortunate enough to find a run earliest. April Diamond's jockey Greg Fairley's positional awareness and King Sharja's inside draw knowledge could prove decisive in traffic, though this scenario depends on unpredictable circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune sets the entire race's rhythm unchallenged — if she is allowed to bowl along at her own pace without a single horse testing her early, the gallop could be slow enough for her to hold on and the hold-up runners may simply not have enough race to run at.|

The sheer volume of hold-up horses — King Sharja, Monhammer, Misemerald, Wait For It, April Diamond and Sanditon all tracking the same leader — creates a significant risk of traffic problems and blocked runs in the straight at Musselburgh, where space is at a premium.|

Sanditon and Misemerald are the two redistributed hold-up types most likely to push forward and race prominently against their natural style; if either secures a position just off Braes Of Doune's shoulder early, they avoid the traffic bunching and gain a material tactical edge.|

King Sharja's course form at 7f on good ground (two seconds from recent runs) is the most directly relevant form in the race — watch how James Sullivan positions him leaving the stalls, as getting clear of the hold-up cluster early will be critical to delivering his finish.|

Wait For It runs for the second time in nine days and her best form has come over six furlongs rather than seven — monitor market moves to assess whether connections are confident she stays this trip strongly enough to compete with hold-up horses who have stronger profiles at the distance.|

races.name: Lens Self Storage Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with placed efforts at 13f and 17f on Good ground (2nd, 3rd), handled by Greg Fairley for Ewan Whillans whose yard is 4 from 10 over 14 days; tongue-tie and hood combination noted, but the 18-day gap is manageable and she stays the trip.
runners_data.comment: Inappropriate has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out and second four starts back, with going experience in his favour and a race-fit 18-day turnaround lending further appeal; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Teofimo
runners_data.note: 40 days off the track for Adam Nicol's yard which has managed just 0 from 2 in that window; a natural hold-up type whose best form came at 20f on Good (3rd), and he'll need luck in running from the rear in what is a very congested tail-end of the field.
runners_data.comment: Teofimo posted a second three starts back on today's going, and our rating has him as the one to beat in this field — but he's winless in his last four starts and back-to-back eighths and sevenths demand respect for those shortcomings.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Recent form shows back-to-back wins on Tapeta at Southwell (12f, 16f), but this switch to Good turf at Musselburgh is an unknown quantity — genuinely a hold-up horse who will be racing further forward than he'd like given the traffic at the rear of this field, which tempers confidence despite strong current form.
runners_data.comment: Clansman landed a win two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, but a below-par effort last time tempers expectations, and he carries 131 lb off a rating of 71.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: One win and five places from 15 runs on Good ground underlines his consistency at this level; an authentic hold-up performer by nature, he will be squeezed into a midfield role against his instincts, which historically limits his best finishes — David Nolan must find a way through on the final bend.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third four starts back, Arrange has shown she can hit the frame and her experience over today's trip and going is a plus; winless in her last five starts is the caveat, but at 129 lb she looks an interesting each-way proposition fresh off a 39-day break.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 starts on Good, including a fine 2nd at 16f on Good recently, shows she handles the conditions; Gary Rutherford's horse is a true rear-division type by preference, and having to fill a mid-division slot in a race already bursting with similar profiles makes clean passage the central question.
runners_data.comment: Simple Star has run over today's trip and going, shaped with promise when second two starts back, and at 128 lb steps out on a snappy 18-day turnaround with his rating of 73 giving him a competitive edge — though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: The best recent form in the race — a win at 16f Good and a win at 15f Soft — gives him genuine claims if Jake Dickson's 5lb claim keeps the weight competitive; a natural hold-up horse who will be positioned in the pack, but his finishing kick on similar ground makes him the most dangerous of the closers if he gets daylight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Gallus Norman is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last five starts; he has experience of today's distance and going, and a 42-day absence at least means he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Set to lead by default having been redistributed from a prominent/hold-up profile to the front due to the absence of any natural pace-setter; two wins and multiple places at 14–17f on Good and Soft suggest stamina is not in question, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim lightens the load — the key unknown is whether she can sustain a solo gallop over 2m without being run down.
runners_data.comment: Cascade Hall has placed on three of his last four starts — third last time out — and has run over today's distance and going before, so conditions aren't unknown; but ranked sixth of seven on our figures, he faces a stiff task against stronger-rated rivals here.

races.paceDynamic: Cascade Hall is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 2m handicap, having been redistributed from a prominent/hold-up role to the front because no natural front-runner exists in the field — she will effectively dictate from the break at Musselburgh's tight track, setting a controlled, uncontested gallop on Good ground. Behind her, Inappropriate, Teofimo, Clansman, Arrange, Simple Star, and Gallus Norman are all genuine hold-up or rear-division types competing for positions further back, meaning the race will settle into a strung-out, steady-tempo procession with the field locked up behind a moderate pace through the early stages. The real contest will ignite in the straight as several closers attempt to run down Cascade Hall, but with the pace unlikely to be truly searching over two miles, those who can race nearer the tempo will have a meaningful energy advantage over pure hold-up performers. This race shape most favours horses capable of travelling prominently or making a forward move before the final bend, as a controlled pace rewards those who do not burn deep reserves chasing from far off the pace — the field holds far more hold-up types than can realistically get a good run, with Clansman, Arrange, and Simple Star most likely squeezed out of their natural positions and denied their ideal race shape.

watchPoints.text: Cascade Hall is leading on borrowed terms — watch how comfortably Lauren Young settles her in front, because if she fights for her head or quickens too soon on the tight Musselburgh circuit, she will be vulnerable to every closer in the final two furlongs.

Gallus Norman enters the straight as the most dangerous threat: Jake Dickson must avoid getting locked behind traffic at the home bend, as his finishing kick on Good ground is proven at this sort of trip and he could arrive too late if impeded.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Clansman, Arrange, Simple Star — will all be competing for the same ground in the straight; watch for potential interference or traffic issues between them as they attempt to deliver finishing runs from similar positions.

Inappropriate carries a tongue-tie and hood combination — watch whether she travels kindly early under Greg Fairley, as those headgear choices suggest she can be keen, and over 2m on Good ground that could cost her at the business end.

Teofimo is 40 days since his last run and his trainer Adam Nicol has returned just 0 from 2 runners in the past fortnight — watch him closely in the preliminaries and early exchanges for signs of racecourse freshness that could compromise his position from the rear of the field.

races.name: Graham + Sibbald And Neilsons Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: Has won twice over this exact 5f Good-ground combination recently and carries the form to confirm favouritism; Jake Dickson's 5lb claim softens the weight burden and she is the only natural front-runner in the field, making her tactical role entirely straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Pearl arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second before that, bringing smart recent momentum into this; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and the main risk is whether 139 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners a mare who has found the frame four times in her last five runs, all at 5f on Good ground — the form is solid even if she remains a maiden; her naturally prominent style means she will contest early position with Thornaby Pearl, a battle she may not win cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite three runner-up finishes, Thunderstorm Katie has struggled to convert and ranks fifth of six on our figures; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 20 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh, but she remains hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Harry Burns (3lb claimer) partners a horse whose entire recent profile is on Standard artificial tracks rather than turf, making this Good-ground 5f turf assignment a notable surface switch; four consecutive places on the all-weather suggest consistency but the change of surface warrants caution.
runners_data.comment: Peregrine Falcon has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third last time out and third and second in recent starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — though winless in her last five, the chief concern is whether she can finally convert that placed form into something more.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on a 3yo who has been remarkably consistent, placing in six of his last six starts, including twice on Good ground at 5f; the hood is fitted for the first time and, with Michael Dods in strong 14-day form, the visor effect is worth factoring into any late-race assessment.
runners_data.comment: Golden Havana has been a model of consistency, placing second three times in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's distance and going — drawn in stall three carrying 135 lb, he is the one to side with, albeit still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners a hold-up type whose recent form figures on Good ground read 6-9-4-7-12 — the finishing position hides repeated place-seeking runs but deep hold-up tactics have repeatedly left him vulnerable at this trip; his true style is rear-of-field, though the congested field shape pushes him into a midfield map position he would not naturally choose.
runners_data.comment: South Parade shaped with a shade of promise when fourth three starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 66 suggests she's capable of threatening here — yet winless in her last six starts and a trainer firing at just 3% lately are real negatives.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Ran just four days ago and carries headgear (hood), which for a naturally front-running type suggests connections want her switched on early — but the short turnaround combined with her prominent instincts being squeezed out by Thornaby Pearl makes her task harder than the low weight implies; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a practical positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with a string of fourth-place finishes, Wee Mary heads here just four days after her latest effort and ranks last on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one is hers to use.

races.paceDynamic: Thornaby Pearl is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead, she should settle into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the gates on this flat 5f track at Musselburgh. Thunderstorm Katie and Wee Mary are both naturally prominent types who will want to press forward, but with Thornaby Pearl already filling that role, they face a fight for position that may cost them energy in the early stages. This field contains more pace than the race shape can accommodate — Wee Mary and South Parade are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively who have been mapped to midfield positions because they are unlikely to secure their natural ground against the runners ahead of them. A sustainable, uncontested lead at true Good-ground pace sets this race up for a front-runner or a close-tracking prominent type to dictate throughout, meaning horses who can race within striking range of Thornaby Pearl without burning reserves in a positional battle are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thornaby Pearl Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl breaks cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead, controlling pace throughout on this flat 5f course.
scenarios.body: She sets an honest but sustainable gallop on Good ground, denying any rival the chance to unsettle her rhythm, and the front rail becomes her ally to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Force Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Thunderstorm Katie or Wee Mary push hard for position early and force a contested, faster-than-ideal tempo.
scenarios.body: A scrappy early battle for the front rank stretches the field and burns off the natural front-runner, opening the door for a strong finisher tracking in behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the leaders tie each other up, creating a flat-out gallop that sets up the closers.
scenarios.body: Golden Havana and Peregrine Falcon, both consistent place-getters at this trip, get a true target to aim at in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Tight Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively modest and runners bunch approaching the final furlong, turning this into a sprint finish from a tight group.
scenarios.body: South Parade, though racing out of natural role, and Wee Mary could benefit from a blanket finish where positional disadvantage is nullified.

watchPoints.text: Thornaby Pearl's break from the stalls is critical — if she exits cleanly and hits the front without interference, she controls the race tempo entirely and the field is chasing a horse in her comfort zone.

Thunderstorm Katie and Wee Mary are both prominent types who will contest the space behind Thornaby Pearl in the first furlong — watch for early crowding or a bump that disrupts either runner's rhythm and burns race-critical energy.

Golden Havana wearing the hood for the first time is an unknown quantity in terms of early behaviour; if the headgear sharpens him into a closer tracking run, his consistent place-finding form becomes dangerous, but if it unsettles him, his chance evaporates quickly over 5f.

Peregrine Falcon's switch from Standard artificial ground to Good turf is the key unknown — his form figures look consistent but every recent run has been on a completely different surface, and the Musselburgh turf track will feel different underfoot to anything in his recent history.
